From the Senna S to Arquibancada, the crowd is packed, a sea of yellow and green.

historicalReferences: Senna's emotional victory in 1991, battling gearbox issues, remains one of the most iconic moments in Formula 1 history at Interlagos.
Who can forget Schumacher's masterclass in the wet in 2006, navigating the treacherous conditions to claim victory?
Massa's near-miss in 2008, only to have the championship snatched away in the final corner, is etched in the memory of every F1 fan.
The 2012 race was a classic, with Vettel battling back from an early spin to secure his third World Championship.
Lauda's title-clinching fourth place in 1976, after a season of immense pressure, showed his resilience at this famous track.
Prost's dominant victory in 1982 showcased his incredible talent at Interlagos.
Mansell's win in 1989, overcoming a puncture and battling through the field, was a testament to his never-say-die attitude.
Raikkonen's championship win in 2007, a nail-biting finish which saw him clinch the title by a single point.
Alonso's victory in 2006, a commanding performance from start to finish, showed his dominance at the time.
The 1993 race, with Senna's superb drive in the wet, is remembered as one of his greatest victories.
cornerCallouts: The Senna S is crucial, a good exit sets you up perfectly for the long run down to Curva do Sol.
They'll need to be brave into Turn 4, the Descida do Lago, a tricky braking zone that's easy to get wrong.
A slight lift into Ferradura, Turn 7, but the drivers will be pushing the limits of grip through there.
Pinheiro, Turn 9, is a key overtaking spot; drivers often try a late dive down the inside.
The acceleration zone out of Bico de Pato, Turn 11, is vital for setting up a move into Junção.
They're flat out through the Arquibancada, Turns 12 and 13; a real test of nerve and car balance.
The long, sweeping left-hander of Curva do Café, Turn 1, can really punish the tires, especially on a long stint.
A good run through Mergulho, Turn 14, is essential to carry speed onto the Reta Oposta.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a major factor here at Interlagos, especially with the high-speed corners and abrasive surface on this 4.309km layout.
The pit lane is relatively short here, so the pit stop loss isn't as significant compared to other circuits, making multiple stops a viable option.
Fuel management can be tricky, especially in the early stages of the race; drivers will need to balance performance with conservation on this classic layout.
With the unpredictable weather, teams need to be ready to react quickly to changing conditions with the right tire choice.
The long run down to Turn 1 offers overtaking opportunities at the start, but also increases the risk of incidents.
Undercut can be powerful here, with a clean out-lap potentially gaining significant track position on this short 4.309km track.
The high altitude can affect engine performance, so teams will need to optimize their engine maps for the conditions.
A safety car period can dramatically change the race, so teams need to be flexible with their strategy and ready to adapt.
weatherCommentary: The ever-present threat of rain looms large over Interlagos; the microclimate here can make conditions incredibly unpredictable.
The wind can often change direction here, affecting the car balance and making it difficult for the drivers to find consistency.
The humidity is high, making it tough on the drivers in the cockpit, especially during a long race.
The sun is beating down intensely, pushing track temperatures up and affecting tire performance.
That dark cloud is looming over the circuit; it looks like we could be in for a wet race.

"We've been working hard on our setup for this classic layout; tire management will be key to a good result," comments Charles Leclerc.
"The atmosphere here is electric; I'm really looking forward to getting out there and giving it my all," states Lewis Hamilton.
"We know it's going to be a tough race; the competition is fierce, but we're ready for the challenge," says George Russell.
"Interlagos is one of my favorite tracks; it's fast, flowing, and requires a lot of commitment," notes Lando Norris.
"We've got some upgrades on the car this weekend; hopefully, they'll help us to close the gap to the front," says Fernando Alonso.
"The weather is always a factor here; we need to be prepared for anything that comes our way," comments Carlos Sainz.
"I'm really excited to be racing at Interlagos; it's a legendary circuit with a rich history," says Oscar Piastri.
